title: Gebratener welscher Hahn (Roasted Turkey)
description: Prepared with turkey, cherry, and onion.
steps: Before slaughter, pour a glass of cherry spirit into the bird so it runs well into the body.
After bleeding out, let it twitch on the ground.
Pluck warm but do not eviscerate.
Wrap in cloth and set aside until the next day.
Carefully remove the crop with innards, loosen the breastbone, and cut the legs from both sides at the joint, loosening carefully at the breast.
Wash clean and half-chop the feet.
Salt and pepper well.
Using a trussing needle, truss so the breast stands up nicely.
Prepare the stuffing for the crop: cut liver and gizzard (removing the tough skin) into small square pieces.
Braise these with onion and parsley in a piece of butter in a casserole for half an hour.
Meanwhile, cut a fresh roll (removing the crust).
Mix the braised mixture with the roll, add 1/2 schoppen thick sour cream, 3 beaten eggs, and nutmeg to taste.

title: Gedämpfter Fasan (Steamed Pheasant)

Cover the casserole tightly so no steam escapes and braise slowly for 15 minutes.

In a brass pan, braise the minced shallots in a piece of butter until golden.
Let 1 tablespoon flour cook briefly in the pan, then add the mixture from the casserole in which the pheasant braised.
Cook together for 15 minutes.
Add the juice of 1 lemon.

title: Gefrorenes (Frozen Dessert)
description: Prepared with ice, water, and salt.
steps: Crush the ice as finely as possible
Place a hand's height of ice in the freezing bucket and mix in a portion of salt
Set the covered tin or tin plate with the mixture into the bucket
Crush the remaining ice very finely, mix it with salt, and completely cover the tin with it
Sprinkle several handfuls of salt on top to accelerate freezing
Let the tin stand in the ice for only a quarter hour and shake it several times by the handle, ensuring it remains in the ice

Open the lid and insert the stirring spoon with one hand while driving the tin around the spoon with the other hand as quickly as possible, all while keeping it in the ice, as this is very important so that the mass not only freezes faster but also becomes fine and tender
Take care that no ice falls into the tin; wrap a clean cloth around the tin instead
During the stirring, work the bottom and sides of the tin well so that any frozen deposits continually detach
If the frozen mass adheres too strongly, loosen it with the stirring spoon and press it upward in small pieces
Then let the tin stand for a quarter hour, stir and work the mass until the frozen substance is stiff but not lumpy, rather such that it can be cut like butter
Finally close the tin, cover it, let it stand in the bucket, and set it in the cellar
When the mass is firmly frozen, this ice will keep for 3 to 4 hours
When serving, turn it out onto a plate

Let it cook until it forms threads
Press the almonds through linen cloth so they are completely dry

Let everything cook together for 2 minutes

Put it in the freezing tin

Mince 6 shallot onions, the zest of one lemon, basil, thyme, parsley, and tarragon very finely and steam them in a piece of butter.

steps: Wash the tongue and cook it in salt water until not too soft

Grate a kreuzers worth of bread, soak it in water and press it out firmly, add it to the minced meat
Mince half a lemon, steam an onion with fat, and add both to the mixture along with salt, nutmeg, and pepper to taste
Work everything together with one egg until well combined
Fill the tongue with this mixture and tie it together with string
Place it in a saucepan with some lard slices, onions, a bay leaf, and a piece of lemon, cover, and steam for half an hour

Cook 1 pound macaroni in salted water until half-soft, drain well through a sieve

title: Gefüllter Wildschweinskopf (Stuffed Wild Boar Head)
description: Prepared with meat, bacon, and bread.
steps: Cut the head not too short and wash it 2 to 3 times in warm water.
Brush it clean until it becomes a nice yellow color.
Clean the ears thoroughly and cut open the bottom of the head.
Carefully remove the skull so that no holes are made in the skin.
Chop 2 pounds of lean wild boar meat and the meat removed from the head with 1 pound of fresh bacon and mix to a paste.

Soak white bread (roll or semmel) with the crust removed in water, press it firmly out, and work it together with the pork forcemeat, 2 eggs, salt, pepper, cloves, mace, and nutmeg in a mortar until foamy.
Fill half of this mixture into the head, lay some thinly sliced truffles on top, then add the other half of the forcemeat.
Place a piece of bacon rind on top of the stuffing before the opening to keep the filling secure.
Sew the opening closed and wrap the head in cloth.

For the aspic: put 8 cleaned calf's feet, 2 pig's feet, an old hen, 2 pounds of beef or cow meat, all sorts of roots and herbs, cloves, pepper, mace, whole cinnamon, onions, bay leaves, and a generous handful of salt into a well-tinned copper pot.
Pour in 3 measures of wine, 4 measures of water, and 1.5 measures of vinegar.
Place everything together with the pig's head on the fire, cover the pot, cook the head slowly, and turn it often.
A large pig's head often takes 3 to 3.5 hours to cook through.
Place the cooked head on a dish to drain; pour the drained liquid back into the aspic and let it stand overnight if time allows.
Beat 4 eggs into a casserole, carefully remove the fat from the aspic, pour the settled part into the casserole, put it on the fire, and whisk with a whisk until it begins to boil.
Remove it from heat, squeeze the juice of a lemon into it, and strain it through a felt hat; if it does not become clear on the first straining, filter it through the felt until it is clear enough.
Pour some of this clear aspic onto the plate on which the head is to be served and let it set.
Make a green aspic: crush 2 to 3 handfuls of cleaned spinach in a mortar, press the juice through a cloth, let it coagulate in a small vessel on the fire, and pour it through a fine sieve.
Stir this spinach cheese into half-set aspic, pour it onto the plate so that it forms a mound, and let it set.
Clean the pig's head of all fat and lay it on the mound of green aspic.
Cover it with clear aspic until the head is completely embedded in the aspic.
Before serving, garnish it with lemons and cut-out decorative herbs.
For grand tables, the pig's head can also be prepared as follows: 5 pounds of butter and 5 pounds of lard are stirred together for half an hour until they become like pomade.

Make a kind of altar on a large long plate from most of this mass and decorate it with columns formed from the rest of the mass, which can be colored brown with chocolate, yellow with saffron, or green with spinach cheese.
A hunter, pilgrim, or other figure formed from the same mass can be placed between two such columns.
The pig's head is then placed on this altar.

title: Gesulzte Lachsforelle mit Schuppen (Jellied Salmon Trout with Scales)
description: Prepared with salmon, calf's feet, and pork.
steps: Scale a beautiful salmon trout, cut open the belly and remove the entrails

Wipe the slime from the trout and braise in a covered kettle with 1 Schoppen wine, 2 Schoppen water, all kinds of good herbs, and a small handful of salt, braising rather than boiling so it does not burst

Cook the jelly on the fire with 1 Schoppen boiling milk, add the juice of 1 lemon and cook a while longer
Remove from heat and let stand for a quarter hour, then strain through a suspended felt hat

Oil must be added drop by drop, along with some jelly, stirring for 1.5 to 2 hours
Pour onto the plate with the light jelly so that 2 fingers width of light jelly remains visible all around
Let it set firm, carefully pour light jelly over again, make some green jelly and pour it so the fish lies just on the green jelly

title: Gesulzter welscher Hahn (Aspic-Glazed Guinea Fowl)
description: Prepared with fowl, pork, and veal.

ingredients.name: white bread (2 kreuzer worth, crusts removed), soaked in milk and squeezed
1/4 pound bacon, cut into small pieces
zest of 2 lemons, finely chopped, plus the pulp without seeds
1/2 pound ham, cut into quill-feather-thick pieces
1/2 pound bacon, cut into quill-feather-thick pieces
1 whole lemon, cut into leaves, without seeds

steps: Clean the guinea fowl, wash it, remove the eyes, and scald the head to make it white; do not gut it. Cut off the feet at the knuckle, cut the fowl open along the back, and remove the body in such a way that all the meat remains attached to the skin. Cut off the wings at the second joint and cut through the neck so that the head remains attached to the skin. Remove the wing bones.

For the forcemeat: cut the bacon into small pieces and render it in a pan with the chopped onions until they are slightly golden. Mix the pork and veal forcemeat with the bread soaked in milk and squeezed, the cooked onions and bacon, salt, cloves, mace, nutmeg, lemon zest and pulp, anchovies, and truffles. Grind everything together in a mortar with 2 eggs and 2 egg yolks until it forms a foam.

Fill one quarter of the forcemeat into the guinea fowl, then layer half a pound of ham and half a pound of bacon cut into quill-feather-thick pieces with truffle slices. Add another layer of forcemeat, then another layer of ham, bacon, and truffle, finishing with a layer of forcemeat. Make sure to fill the neck and thighs well with forcemeat.
Sew up the fowl, tuck the head under the wing, and wrap it tightly in clean cloth to maintain its shape.

Place the prepared fowl in a large pan with 8 chopped veal feet, add 1 measure of wine, 2 measures of water, and 3 schoppen of vinegar. Add 1 loth of mace, 1 whole lemon cut into leaves without seeds, 2 yellow turnips cut into pieces, 4 bay leaves, 4 onions, 1 celery cut into pieces, and cloves and pepper totaling 1 loth.
Cook everything for 2 to 3 hours. If the broth does not cover the fowl, add more water and wine. After 2 hours, remove the fowl and let it cool in the cloth.
Continue cooking the remaining ingredients for another hour. Strain through a fine sieve into a clean vessel and let stand overnight.

On the day of serving, remove the fat from the aspic, bring the aspic to a boil in a pan, crush 3 whole eggs into it, and stir until it boils. Remove from heat, add the juice of 3 lemons, and strain through a felt hat.
Remove the cloth from the fowl, clean it with a clean cloth, place it on a platter, and cover with clear aspic. Let it cool, then cover again, repeating until the fowl is completely covered in aspic.
Garnish with bay leaves and lemons.

ingredients.name: cinnamon, cloves, anise, figs, 1 glass cherry spirit
wheat flour and some beer yeast

steps: Boil medlars and plums
Add raisins as desired
Cut blanched almonds lengthwise
Break walnuts into 50-60 pieces
Combine with spices and cherry spirit
Mix wheat flour and beer yeast with cooked medlar broth
Make a starter dough and let it rise in warmth
When ripe, work it together thoroughly and salt it
Let it rise again until half-risen
Form into loaves
Work in the spiced medlars
Brush loaves with medlar broth
Let them rise once more
Bake in the oven

title: Gänsebraten, Fetter (Rich Roast Goose)
description: Prepared with goose, apples, and onions.
steps: Prepare the goose according to instructions; remove wings, neck, head and feet.
Carefully separate the intestinal fat from the other fat and soak both separately.
After the goose is washed and dried, rub it with salt.

Peel or leave unpeeled the apples as desired, cut them or if small leave them whole, toss with sugar and salt and fill the goose with them along with the rinsed mugwort; sew it closed and rub salt on the outside.
Keep the oven not too hot in the first hour, pour 1/2 l boiling water over the goose; add onions and spice mixture.
Baste the goose with water for 1 hour in the oven. In the first hour you should notice neither color nor roasting aroma; if the oven temperature rises, cover the goose with parchment paper.
After about 1 hour, the goose will have rendered enough of its own fat to baste with; fill with spoonfuls of water from time to time so the fat doesn't brown.
After 1-1/2 hours, occasionally skim fat from the sauce and roast the goose to a nice brown color.

When tender, sprinkle it with 1 spoonful of cold water so the skin becomes crispy, arrange the goose and cook the sauce in the pan with some water and potato starch stirred in water to sufficient consistency, and can also color with food coloring.
Pour the sauce through a fine sieve.

title: Hasenbraten für 6 Personen (Roasted Hare for 6 Persons)
description: Prepared with hare, bacon, and margarine.

ingredients.name: 1/4 liter sour cream or milk, or milk with 1 drop of vinegar

steps: Hang the hare by its hind legs on 2 hooks or strong nails; if not yet eviscerated, cut open the body lengthwise from the tail, remove the entrails with the rectum, separate the gallbladder from the liver, keep the liver, heart and lungs, discard the rest, loosen the fur on the belly from the skin, cut around the paws with a sharp knife, pull the paws out of the skin, pull the entire pelt over the back and hindquarters, remove it at the front legs, cut off the ears and pull the skin over the head. Cut off the head, neck, and back; remove the belly skin and front legs, skin the legs and braise them later. Leave the kidneys and fat in the hare, then wash it thoroughly in cold water without soaking. Cut off the hind legs at the joint, break the tailbone so the hindquarters lie well, beat the hare everywhere with a flat mallet, skin it, first the hindquarters from the underside likewise the back, either remove the fillets or place 1 slice of bacon underneath and lard the hare and legs.

Once everything is prepared, first place the hindquarters in the roasting pan and, so the roast does not dry out, 15 minutes later add the back and the bent-in legs, sprinkle the hare with salt and pour hot margarine over it. After the hare has browned, gradually pour in the sour cream or milk and some hot water alternately and let it finish roasting with frequent basting. Meanwhile, stir cornstarch and a few spoonfuls of sour cream or milk into the sauce, coat the hare with it after a few minutes and arrange it on a long platter after it has been cut into appropriate pieces (one can also bring the whole hare to table and separate the meat in clean pieces to still use the bone framework for a soup); deglaze the roasting pan with sour cream or milk until the sauce becomes thick and glossy and strain it through a fine sieve into a gravy boat, pouring a few spoonfuls over the arranged hare. The length of roasting time and heat naturally depends on whether the hare is young or old; a young full-grown hare would become tender at medium heat in 35 minutes, the back in 25 minutes, an old hare at lower temperature only in 1-1/2 hours. In the latter case, cover it with butcher paper.

description: A sauce made with game, vinegar, and lard.

ingredients.name: Game meat, preferably from the hind leg

One cleaned and finely ground truffle

steps: Marinate the game meat in vinegar for a few days beforehand.
Skin the meat well and lard it; pour hot lard over it.
Line the bottom of a casserole with onions, bacon, all kinds of roots, bay leaves, 6 whole cloves, mace, whole white peppercorns, and cubebs and cardamom (totaling half a loth).

Place all the game meat in the casserole, pour a glass of wine and a ladleful of meat broth over it, cover the casserole tightly (or better yet, seal it with paper), place it on coals, and let it steam slowly for 2 to 3 hours.
Do not salt it until serving time.
For the sauce: Rub one quarter pound Nuremberg gingerbread and the same amount of black bread on a grater.
Roast the grated mixture in a piece of pork fat along with a small piece of sugar until it looks brown like gingerbread.
Pour a quart of wine and 2 ladles full of good bouillon over it and let it cook together.
Place the game meat on a dish to keep warm, pass the juice through a fine sieve, and pour it into the sauce.
Put the meat and sauce into another casserole, cut 6 to 8 mushrooms into small pieces, add one spoonful of capers and one cleaned and finely ground truffle.
Let everything cook together for another quarter hour, and when serving, squeeze the juice of half a lemon over it and sprinkle the grated zest on the game.

Complete the roast by mixing 3 tablespoons milk or water with potato flour, cook it out with the sauce, strain through a sieve, and coat the knuckle with the sauce.
If preferring well-done rather than pink meat, allow 10 minutes per half kilogram (1 Pfd.).

steps: Take 4 pounds flour in a bowl with 4 strong tablespoons beer yeast and 3 schoppen warm milk and make a very strong dough

Work everything again until no flour is visible

Cover it so it does not form a skin

Roll them out finger-long, dust a black sheet with flour, place them side by side to the end, let the dough rise once more in warmth
Brush with beaten egg and bake in the oven until beautifully golden, but do not cut them until the third day

title: Kirschenpudding (Cherry Pudding)
description: A pudding made with cherry, rolls, and blanched almonds.
steps: Cut the rind from 3 white rolls, soak them, press them out, pound 1/4 pound blanched almonds with egg white.

Fill the mass into a damp cloth, tie it closed firmly, cook the pudding one hour in boiling water.

title: Kohlrabi (Kohlrabi)
description: Prepared with fat or margarine, salt, and water.
steps: Set 1 l water with 10 g salt to boil; wash the young greens of the kohlrabi; peel the bulbs and cut into uniform slices.
